scope: Audit of the current HSConfig source-contract and apply-gate implementation for any-deck no-block autonomy under unsupported future mechanics, thin guide evidence, runtime-evidence-only GlobalValues requests, source-to-runtime gaps, unresolved option identities, source claim conflicts, stale plan-report metadata, and diagnostic-only claim/report surfaces.
verified_strengths: The normal runtime-write authority remains singular. docs/operator/README.md and src/hsconfig/operator_summary.py keep reports/operator_summary.json as the only normal apply authority, and src/hsconfig/apply_gate.py reads that summary plus concrete package-structure checks instead of consulting diagnostic reports as independent gates.

Valid warning-bearing packages still apply. src/hsconfig/operator_summary.py maps VALID_PACKAGE plus non-BLOCKED apply policy to runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply, and tests/test_apply_gate.py proves VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, source-gap, runtime-surface-gap, and thin-usefulness packages remain allowed when the runtime package is structurally sound.

Unsupported future mechanics stay visible without becoming apply blockers. src/hsconfig/mechanic_support.py classifies unknown or unmapped mechanics as warning_only/report-only, src/hsconfig/mechanic_drift.py emits non_blocking drift summaries, and tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py proves future_mechanic visibility remains warning-only while runtime_apply_mode stays load_safe_apply.

Thin guide evidence remains visible but non-blocking. src/hsconfig/config_usefulness.py sets runtime_permission_impact=none and blocking=false, while src/hsconfig/no_block_failure_modes.py keeps source_depth_warning and guide_strength_gap in follow-up categories instead of hard-stop categories.

Runtime-evidence-only GlobalValues requests are preserved as visible debt rather than apply blockers. src/hsconfig/source_document_model.py rejects globalvalue_numeric_tuning from Step 1 lowering with requires_runtime_evidence, src/hsconfig/globalvalues_authority.py records those keys under blocked_until_runtime_evidence with claim references, and tests/test_source_contract_audit.py plus tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py verify the resulting lifecycle rows are suppressed with first_missing_link=runtime_evidence and operator_impact=diagnostic_only.

Source-to-runtime gaps remain explicit without becoming a second gate. src/hsconfig/source_contract_audit.py and src/hsconfig/source_to_runtime_explainability.py emit diagnostic-only summaries with next_report_to_open links, while src/hsconfig/operator_summary.py exposes those summaries as non_blocking visibility only.

Unresolved option identities are suppressed instead of blocking valid packages. src/hsconfig/card_behavior_surface_router.py emits unresolved_option_identity suppression for discover and choose-one claims, lowers only resolved choices, and tests/test_card_behavior_router.py proves resolved choices emit while unresolved choices stay non-emitted.

Source claim conflicts are quarantined instead of promoted to apply blockers. src/hsconfig/source_claim_conflicts.py downgrades contradictory claim families to report-visible conflicts, src/hsconfig/source_claim_lifecycle.py marks affected claims quarantined, and tests/test_source_contract_audit.py plus tests/test_source_claim_quality_autonomy.py verify quarantined claims become suppressed_quarantined_claim rows while the package remains VALID_PACKAGE and load_safe_apply.

Stale or report-only expert plan-report rows are filtered through lifecycle claim eligibility before runtime emission. src/hsconfig/package_builder.py filters imported mulligan, card-behavior, combo, and GlobalValues rows by allowed lifecycle claim IDs, and tests/test_cli.py proves stale report-only, low-confidence, rejected combo, and quarantined conflict rows do not emit runtime rows even when they exist in plan reports.

Diagnostic-only boundaries are actively defended. tests/test_no_second_gate_contract.py, tests/test_apply_authority_boundary.py, and tests/test_contract_spine_sentinel.py verify that source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, contract_spine_rows, and claim_lifecycle_rows do not gain apply authority, and that report ownership still names only reports/operator_summary.json as the gate.

Representative any-deck proof is still present. tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py covers twelve valid Wild decks and verifies VALID_PACKAGE, runtime_load_safe=true, runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply, runtime_apply_allowed=true, non-blocking diagnostic summaries, required minimal runtime files, rich per-card output, and no normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json.

correctness_gaps: No confirmed current correctness gap was found in the audited any-deck no-block autonomy path.

source_contract_audit.py intentionally treats policy-matrix failure as non-blocking diagnostic degradation by falling back to unsupported_or_unmapped lanes. That preserves operator autonomy, but developer drift could be hidden from normal package consumers unless contract-spine sentinel or CI tests keep running.

The expert --plan-reports-dir path depends on lifecycle claim IDs and claim_refs to distinguish fresh runtime-candidate rows from stale report-only or quarantined rows. If future builders stop preserving those references, stale-row filtering could silently become less precise even though the current tests cover the guarded path.

The apply gate intentionally trusts technical validation plus generated-file accounting rather than semantic strength. That is correct for no-block autonomy, but any future weakening of validation_report or generated_files truthfulness would turn into a real correctness risk.
slimness_gaps: The workflow stays slim only if operator_summary.json remains the one normal decision surface. Promoting source_contract_audit, explainability, contract-doctor, acceptance-matrix, or source-informed summaries into parallel approval surfaces would recreate duplicate authority.

The no-block contract stays lean only if minimal runtime apply remains limited to GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json. Treating per-card CardID coverage, combo richness, source-backed-strong promotion, or exact option identity as mandatory apply prerequisites would bloat the base package model.

The expert inspected path must remain clearly separate from the normal path. If --plan-reports-dir, legacy claim ingestion, or developer diagnostics become routine operator requirements, HSConfig would lose its current configure-first simplicity.
autonomy_gaps: Any future change that upgrades warning-only future mechanics, mechanic drift, thin guide evidence, config_usefulness gaps, or source-to-runtime explainability gaps into technical_hard_block would break the current any-deck autonomy promise.

Any future change that turns runtime-evidence-only GlobalValues tuning into a Step 1 hard requirement would block otherwise valid decks that only need baseline posture overlays and visible follow-up tuning debt.

Any future change that treats unresolved option identities or claim conflicts as package-invalidating rather than suppression-worthy would unnecessarily block valid decks instead of producing a thinner but still load-safe package.

Structure drift is still intentionally blocking: mismatched generated_files, nested runtime files, invalid runtime JSON, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, or reintroduced Presume.json/Concede.json will stop apply even if semantic warnings are otherwise non-blocking. That boundary is correct, but it is the main remaining way valid source-thin work can still fail if package generation drifts.
guardrails_to_keep: Keep reports/operator_summary.json as the only normal apply authority and the first report to open.
Keep src/hsconfig/apply_gate.py limited to operator_summary.json plus concrete package-structure and JSON-integrity checks, not diagnostic verdicts.
Keep src/hsconfig/no_block_failure_modes.py with technical_hard_block as the only hard-stop category and all other categories explanatory only.
Keep globalvalue_numeric_tuning suppressed to blocked_until_runtime_evidence, with claim references preserved and warnings surfaced through operator_summary.json.
Keep source_contract_audit.json and source_to_runtime_explainability.json diagnostic-only, with operator_impact/apply_blocking remaining diagnostic_only/false.
Keep unresolved discover and choose-one option identities suppressed unless exact option identity is source-backed.
Keep source claim conflicts quarantined and suppressed rather than runtime-emitted or package-invalidating.
Keep lifecycle-based filtering on imported plan-report rows so stale report-only, low-confidence, rejected, or quarantined rows cannot silently become runtime authority.

Keep warning-only future mechanics, mechanic drift, and source-depth gaps visible through mechanic_visibility_summary, warning_boundaries, mechanic_drift_summary, source_claim_quality_summary, and explainability summaries.
Keep contract-spine sentinel, apply-authority boundary tests, stale plan-report filter tests, option-identity tests, and the universal no-block deck matrix active.
recommended_next_design: Keep the current single-gate no-block design. Do not widen runtime authority beyond reports/operator_summary.json. Preserve lifecycle-based quarantine and stale-row filtering, keep runtime-evidence-only GlobalValues requests and unresolved option identities diagnostic, and add only narrow regression tests when new claim kinds, mechanic buckets, or expert import surfaces are introduced.
